title: Data Scientist Readiness
description: Assess your understanding of statistical inference, machine learning algorithms, cross-validation, feature engineering, and model metrics.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Type I and Type II errors in statistical hypothesis testing?
options: Type I is a False Positive (rejecting a true null hypothesis); Type II is a False Negative (failing to reject a false null)
Type I is a False Negative; Type II is a False Positive
Type I is caused by small sample sizes; Type II is caused by skewed data
Type I only happens in linear regression models
questions.explanation: Type I error (alpha) occurs when you incorrectly reject the null hypothesis; Type II error (beta) occurs when you fail to reject a false null.

questions.question: In classification problems with severe class imbalance (e.g. 99% negative, 1% positive), which evaluation metric is most misleading if used alone?
questions.explanation: A dummy classifier predicting all negatives achieves 99% accuracy while having zero utility for detecting the rare positive class.

questions.question: What problem occurs when a machine learning model has high variance and low bias?
questions.explanation: High variance means the model is overly complex and fits training noise closely (overfitting), failing to generalize to unseen test data.

questions.question: What is the role of Regularization (L1 Lasso and L2 Ridge) in linear models?
options: Penalizing large model coefficients to prevent overfitting and reduce model variance
Speeding up gradient descent by scaling learning rates
Converting non-linear data into binary classes
questions.explanation: Regularization adds a penalty term (L1: absolute weights, L2: squared weights) to the loss function to constrain coefficient magnitude and control complexity.

questions.question: Which algorithm is an ensemble method based on Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating)?
questions.explanation: Random Forest builds multiple independent decision trees on bootstrapped subsets of data and averages their predictions (Bagging).

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Principal Component Analysis (PCA)?
options: Unsupervised linear dimensionality reduction that projects data onto orthogonal axes of maximum variance
Imputing missing values using nearest neighbors
questions.explanation: PCA finds principal component vectors that maximize variance and minimize reconstruction error for dimensionality reduction.

questions.question: In Scikit-Learn, why must the scaler (e.g. `StandardScaler`) be fitted ONLY on the training split (`fit_transform`) and only applied (`transform`) to the test split?
options: To prevent Data Leakage from the test set into the model training pipeline
Because Scikit-Learn throws an error if fit is called twice
To balance the test dataset labels
questions.explanation: Fitting on test data leaks test distribution parameters (mean/variance) into training, producing overly optimistic and biased evaluations.

questions.question: What is SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) used for in modern data science?
options: Explaining model predictions by computing the game-theoretic marginal contribution of each feature
Compressing neural network weights into 8-bit integers
Running unit tests on database queries
questions.explanation: SHAP provides unified interpretability for any machine learning model based on cooperative game theory Shapley values.

questions.question: What is the Elbow Method used for in K-Means clustering?
options: Determining the optimal number of clusters (k) by plotting within-cluster sum of squares (inertia)
Detecting multivariate outliers in regression models
Selecting the learning rate for gradient descent
questions.explanation: The Elbow Method plots inertia against k to spot the bend point where adding more clusters yields diminishing returns.

questions.question: What statistical test is most appropriate to determine if there is a significant association between two categorical variables in a contingency table?
questions.explanation: The Chi-Square test of independence compares observed and expected frequencies across categorical contingency tables.
